Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Semarang City.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Semarang.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of Almighty God and constitute His gift which must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, government, and every person for the sake of the honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
6. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
7. Protection of Women is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender difference that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain acts, arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
9. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society.
10. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development.

Point a

What is meant by "The principle of respect for human rights" contains the understanding that the Republic of Indonesia recognizes and upholds human rights and fundamental human freedoms as rights that are inherently attached to and inseparable from humans, which must be protected, respected, and upheld for the enhancement of human dignity, welfare, happiness, and intelligence as well as justice.

Point b

What is meant by "The principle of non-discrimination" is that in providing protection to women and children victims of violence, there shall be no distinction on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Point c

What is meant by "The principle of gender equality and justice" is that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. What is meant by "The principle of inclusion" is that the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is carried out by inviting and involving all people with various diversities of abilities, backgrounds, characteristics, status, conditions, ethnicity, culture and others as well as facilitating special needs based on such diversity and eliminating barriers that may hinder the equality of every woman in obtaining her rights.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, enhance participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society to improve the quality of women's lives.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 23

(1) Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data based on laws and regulations.

(2) Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be implemented with working groups and/or integrated services established by Mayor's Decree.

(3) Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection.

Article 29

(1) The Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection shall function as the leading sector in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.

(2) Further provisions regarding the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VI

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION STRATEGY

Article 30

(1) The community, community groups/community organizations, business sector, academics, and/or other professional groups may participate in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.

(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:

a. cooperation;
b. synergy;
c. provision of communication, information and education media on Women's Empowerment and Protection; and
d. active role in the fulfillment of women's rights through social responsibility.
(3) Further provisions regarding participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

Part Four

Institutional Strengthening of Women's Protection

Article 31

(1) The Mayor through the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection shall conduct guidance and supervision over Women's Empowerment and Protection;

(2) Forms of guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) are as follows: a.providing socialization to the community and business sector regarding Women's Empowerment and Protection policies; b.providing educational media on Women's Empowerment and Protection, and other related issues and disseminating them to the community; c.facilitating capacity building of institutions implementing Women's Empowerment and Protection; d.facilitating forums for women's participation and women's organizations; e.coordinating the participation of the business sector and other institutions, and international assistance for Women's Empowerment and Protection; and

f. providing awards to the community and business sector both individually and institutionally that have made efforts in Women's Empowerment and Protection.

(3) Form of supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of monitoring and evaluation activities on Women's Empowerment and Protection.

(4) The Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection shall report the results of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) to the Mayor.

Point a

Sufficiently clear.

Point b

What is meant by the basic rights of workers include:

a. the basic right to obtain fair wages.
b. the right to obtain equal opportunities and treatment from the company without discrimination.
c. the right to obtain work training to improve and develop work competence. d. the right to perform work according to the specified time.
e. the right to labor placement.
f. the right to obtain protection for occupational health and safety.
g. the right to obtain welfare through labor social security.
h. the right to participate in trade unions or labor unions.
i. the right to obtain leave: at least 12 working days after the employee has worked for one year continuously.
j. the right to rest: workers after working four hours continuously, shall have the opportunity to rest for a minimum of half an hour.
k. the right to maternity leave, miscarriage leave and menstrual leave specifically for female workers/laborers:

Female workers/laborers are entitled to rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife.

Female workers/laborers who experience a miscarriage are entitled to rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months or in accordance with a certificate from an obstetrician or midwife.

Female workers/laborers who experience pain during menstruation and notify the employer, are not obliged to work on the first and second days during menstruation.

l. the right to perform worship.

m. the right to conduct strikes.

n. the right to obtain severance pay in the event of termination of employment or layoffs.

o. the right to a reasonable opportunity to provide breast milk to their child if it must be done during working hours.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, enhance participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society to improve the quality of women's lives.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, enhance participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society to improve the quality of women's lives.

The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, enhance participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society to improve the quality of women's lives.

Point a

What is meant by "The principle of respect for human rights" contains the understanding that the Republic of Indonesia recognizes and upholds human rights and fundamental human freedoms as rights that are inherently attached to and inseparable from humans, which must be protected, respected, and upheld for the enhancement of human dignity, welfare, happiness, and intelligence as well as justice.

What is meant by "The principle of justice and legal certainty" is that it contains the understanding that every person is entitled to recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal treatment as well as legal certainty and equal treatment before the law.

What is meant by "The principle of benefit" is that it contains the understanding that the regulation of women's empowerment policies must provide the greatest benefit for the welfare of society.

Point f

What is meant by "The principle of participation" is that it contains the understanding that the entire process of policy formulation and implementation must take into account the active participation of all components of society so as to obtain equal benefits in all fields of development and life.

Point g

What is meant by "The principle of accountability" is that it relates to the fact that the implementation of women's empowerment must be accountable and is part of the accountability of government implementation.

Point h

What is meant by "The principle of inclusion" is that the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is carried out by inviting and involving all people with various diversities of abilities, backgrounds, characteristics, status, conditions, ethnicity, culture and others as well as facilitating special needs based on such diversity and eliminating barriers that may hinder the equality of every woman in obtaining her rights.

On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

What is meant by "The principle of respect for human rights" contains the understanding that the Republic of Indonesia recognizes and upholds human rights and fundamental human freedoms as rights that are inherently attached to and inseparable from humans, which must be protected, respected, and upheld for the enhancement of human dignity, welfare, happiness, and intelligence as well as justice.

What is meant by "The principle of non-discrimination" is that in providing protection to women and children victims of violence, there shall be no distinction on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Point d

What is meant by "The principle of justice and legal certainty" is that it contains the understanding that every person is entitled to recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal treatment as well as legal certainty and equal treatment before the law.

Point e

What is meant by "The principle of benefit" is that it contains the understanding that the regulation of women's empowerment policies must provide the greatest benefit for the welfare of society.

Point f

What is meant by "The principle of participation" is that it contains the understanding that the entire process of policy formulation and implementation must take into account the active participation of all components of society so as to obtain equal benefits in all fields of development and life.

Point g

What is meant by "The principle of accountability" is that it relates to the fact that the implementation of women's empowerment must be accountable and is part of the accountability of government implementation.

Point h

What is meant by "The principle of inclusion" is that the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is carried out by inviting and involving all people with various diversities of abilities, backgrounds, characteristics, status, conditions, ethnicity, culture and others as well as facilitating special needs based on such diversity and eliminating barriers that may hinder the equality of every woman in obtaining her rights.

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, enhance participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society to improve the quality of women's lives.

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, enhance participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society to improve the quality of women's lives.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, enhance participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society to improve the quality of women's lives.

Article 30

(1) The community, community groups/community organizations, business sector, academics, and/or other professional groups may participate in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.

a. cooperation;
b. synergy;
c. provision of communication, information and education media on Women's Empowerment and Protection; and
d. active role in the fulfillment of women's rights through social responsibility.
(3) Further provisions regarding participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

Article 31

(1) The Mayor through the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection shall conduct guidance and supervision over Women's Empowerment and Protection;

f. providing awards to the community and business sector both individually and institutionally that have made efforts in Women's Empowerment and Protection.

(3) Form of supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of monitoring and evaluation activities on Women's Empowerment and Protection.

(4) The Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection shall report the results of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) to the Mayor.

Article 14

Point a

Sufficiently clear.

Point b

What is meant by the basic rights of workers include:

a. the basic right to obtain fair wages.
b. the right to obtain equal opportunities and treatment from the company without discrimination.
c. the right to obtain work training to improve and develop work competence. d. the right to perform work according to the specified time.
e. the right to labor placement.
f. the right to obtain protection for occupational health and safety.
g. the right to obtain welfare through labor social security.
h. the right to participate in trade unions or labor unions.
i. the right to obtain leave: at least 12 working days after the employee has worked for one year continuously.
j. the right to rest: workers after working four hours continuously, shall have the opportunity to rest for a minimum of half an hour.
k. the right to maternity leave, miscarriage leave and menstrual leave specifically for female workers/laborers:

Female workers/laborers are entitled to rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife.

Female workers/laborers who experience a miscarriage are entitled to rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months or in accordance with a certificate from an obstetrician or midwife.

Female workers/laborers who experience pain during menstruation and notify the employer, are not obliged to work on the first and second days during menstruation.

l. the right to perform worship.

m. the right to conduct strikes.

n. the right to obtain severance pay in the event of termination of employment or layoffs.

o. the right to a reasonable opportunity to provide breast milk to their child if it must be done during working hours.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, enhance participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society to improve the quality of women's lives.

Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.

What is meant by the basic rights of workers include:

a. the basic right to obtain fair wages.
b. the right to obtain equal opportunities and treatment from the company without discrimination.

Female workers/laborers who experience a miscarriage are entitled to rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months or in accordance with a certificate from an obstetrician or midwife.

l. the right to perform worship.

m. the right to conduct strikes.

n. the right to obtain severance pay in the event of termination of employment or layoffs.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, enhance participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society to improve the quality of women's lives.

What is meant by "The principle of respect for human rights" contains the understanding that the Republic of Indonesia recognizes and upholds human rights and fundamental human freedoms as rights that are inherently attached to and inseparable from humans, which must be protected, respected, and upheld for the enhancement of human dignity, welfare, happiness, and intelligence as well as justice.

What is meant by "The principle of non-discrimination" is that in providing protection to women and children victims of violence, there shall be no distinction on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

What is meant by "The principle of gender equality and justice" is that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. (1) The Mayor through the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection shall conduct guidance and supervision over Women's Empowerment and Protection;

f. providing awards to the community and business sector both individually and institutionally that have made efforts in Women's Empowerment and Protection.

NUMBER 7 OF 2023

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, enhance participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society to improve the quality of women's lives.

Point a

What is meant by "The principle of respect for human rights" contains the understanding that the Republic of Indonesia recognizes and upholds human rights and fundamental human freedoms as rights that are inherently attached to and inseparable from humans, which must be protected, respected, and upheld for the enhancement of human dignity, welfare, happiness, and intelligence as well as justice.

What is meant by "The principle of non-discrimination" is that in providing protection to women and children victims of violence, there shall be no distinction on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Point c

What is meant by "The principle of gender equality and justice" is that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Point d

Point e

What is meant by "The principle of benefit" is that it contains the understanding that the regulation of women's empowerment policies must provide the greatest benefit for the welfare of society.

Point f

What is meant by "The principle of participation" is that it contains the understanding that the entire process of policy formulation and implementation must take into account the active participation of all components of society so as to obtain equal benefits in all fields of development and life.

Point g

What is meant by "The principle of accountability" is that it relates to the fact that the implementation of women's empowerment must be accountable and is part of the accountability of government implementation.

Point h

What is meant by "The principle of inclusion" is that the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is carried out by inviting and involving all people with various diversities of abilities, backgrounds, characteristics, status, conditions, ethnicity, culture and others as well as facilitating special needs based on such diversity and eliminating barriers that may hinder the equality of every woman in obtaining her rights.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Semarang City.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Semarang.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of Almighty God and constitute His gift which must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, government, and every person for the sake of the honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
6. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
7. Protection of Women is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender difference that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain acts, arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
9. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society.
10. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development.

Article 31

(1) The Mayor through the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection shall conduct guidance and supervision over Women's Empowerment and Protection;

(2) Forms of guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) are as follows: a.providing socialization to the community and business sector regarding Women's Empowerment and Protection policies; b.providing educational media on Women's Empowerment and Protection, and other related issues and disseminating them to the community; c.facilitating capacity building of institutions implementing Women's Empowerment and Protection; d.facilitating forums for women's participation and women's organizations; e.coordinating the participation of the business sector and other institutions, and international assistance for Women's Empowerment and Protection; and

f. providing awards to the community and business sector both individually and institutionally that have made efforts in Women's Empowerment and Protection.

(3) Form of supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of monitoring and evaluation activities on Women's Empowerment and Protection.

(4) The Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection shall report the results of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) to the Mayor.

(2) Forms of guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) are as follows: a.providing socialization to the community and business sector regarding Women's Empowerment and Protection policies; b.providing educational media on Women's Empowerment and Protection, and other related issues and disseminating them to the community; c.facilitating capacity building of institutions implementing Women's Empowerment and Protection; d.facilitating forums for women's participation and women's organizations; e.coordinating the participation of the business sector and other institutions, and international assistance for Women's Empowerment and Protection; and

f. providing awards to the community and business sector both individually and institutionally that have made efforts in Women's Empowerment and Protection.

(3) Form of supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of monitoring and evaluation activities on Women's Empowerment and Protection.

(4) The Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection shall report the results of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) to the Mayor.

Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
7. Protection of Women is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Governments is to make regional policies to provide services, enhance participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and enduring, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or violated by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall be equal before the law and government and shall uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of status for every citizen, to date women still experience various obstacles to obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the process of policy formulation and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to ensure their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional governments in implementing policies, programs and activities and encourage the institutional capacity of government and society to improve the quality of women's lives.
